issues.description: The exercise specification and template expect an interface named 'Rideable' that declares messageOnRide():String, but the solution repository defines and uses an interface named 'Mountable' with the same method and leaves Rideable.java empty. Concretely: the problem statement UML and the template Main.java refer to 'Rideable' and call messageOnRide() on Rideable references, while solution/src/.../Mountable.java declares the ride method and Pig/Seal implement Mountable (e.g., Pig.java: "implements Mountable", Seal.java: "implements Mountable, Milkable"). Meanwhile solution/src/.../Rideable.java is effectively empty. This naming mismatch between 'Rideable' and 'Mountable' will confuse students and can break automated cross-checking or tests that expect the interface to be named 'Rideable'.
issues.suggestedFix:
Make the interface name consistent across all artifacts. Preferred fixes:
(1) Rename the solution's Mountable interface to Rideable (update file name and declaration to 'public interface Rideable { String messageOnRide(); }'), and update Pig and Seal to implement Rideable; remove the empty Rideable.java file. OR
(2) If Mountable is the intended name, update the problem statement UML and the template (Main.java and description) to use 'Mountable' instead of 'Rideable', and ensure the interface declaration and examples match that name. Ensure the final repository contains a single interface file whose name and declared method match the name used in the problem statement and template so students and tests use the same type.
